 Order

This miscellaneous appeal by the insurance company under Section 173 of Motor Vehicle Act is arising out of the award dated 02.08.2017 passed by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Shajapur in claim case No.53/2014 for exoneration of the appellant from its liability and setting aside the impugned award against the appellant/insurance company.
2. The date of accident and negligence are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the claims tribunal in this regard are not in question.

3. As per the findings of the tribunal, in the case of death of Devi Singh, an amount of compensation to the tune of Rs.5,65,000/- has been awarded by the tribunal with interest from filing of claim petition till realization.

4. Learned counsel for the appellant/insurance company has filed this appeal on the ground that tribunal has committed error in not considering the testimony of Hemchandra Bam (Branch Manager) in which he has stated that owner of offending vehicle bearing registration No.MP09-V- 6703 has been ensured before appellant/insurance company for which amount of premium of Rs.8,099/- was paid by respondent No.7 through Cheque No.487851.
As the pertinent Cheque was produced before Bank of India, Shajapur which was returned due to insufficient funds.
So insurance company cancelled the insurance policy No.320302/31/13/6100002439 of the offending vehicle.
The information of revocation of insurance policy had been given through registered post dated 03.12.2013 before the date of accident and the receipt of which has been produced before the tribunal.
So insurance company is not liable to --3-- pay compensation.
In view of above, tribunal ought not to have drawn adverse inference and ought to have exonerated the appellant/insurance company.

He further stated that insurance policy was revoked by the insurance company due to dishonor of premium cheque because it was mentioned in the insurance policy that "in case of dishonour of premium cheque, this document stands automatically "Ab initio", hence, insurance company must be exonerated.
5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent supported the impugned award and prayed for rejection of the appeal.

6. Heard the learned counsel for both the parties and perused the record.
7.

It is settled principle that after receiving the information that cheque has been dishonoured by the bank, registered notice must be sent by the insurance company to the owner of the vehicle for revocation of insurance policy.
It must be duly served.

In United India Insurance Company Limited Vs. Laxmamma and others, 2012 (II), Accident Claim Case (Supreme Court), it has been held by the Apex Court that notice for revocation of policy must be served upon the owner of the offending National Insurance Co.Ltd. vs Chitibai on 14 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107019078/
2 vehicle before the accident then effect of revocation of policy mus be applicable.
8.

sentences.text: In the present case, witness of insurance company stated in examination in chief that notice for revocation of insurance policy has been sent to owner of the offending vehicle by registered post dated 03.12.2013 i.e. before the date of accident.
On perusal of the record of the tribunal, it is found that insurance company has not filed receipt of the registered post before the tribunal.

He has filed the acknowledgment Ex.D-4 in which no seal was put by the post office by which it was sent --4-- and by whom it was received so this Ex.D-4 is not reliable so tribunal has disbelieved this Ex.D-4.
9.

Perusal of paragraph Nos.9, 10 and 11 of the award of the tribunal, in the considered opinion of this Court, tribunal has rightly found that tribunal has not sent notice to the owner of the offending vehicle before the accident so tribunal has rightly not exonerated the insurance company from its liability and 10.
In view of the aforesaid, no case for interference is made out with the order passed by the claims tribunal.
Hence, the present appeal stands dismissed.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE N.R.
